blocks.explanation:
Pehle shakal ghaur se dekhiye: \(\ln(1 + e^x)\) ke saath \(e^x\) bhi hai, aur \(e^x\) bilkul \(1 + e^x\) ka derivative hai.
Is ka matlab hai substitution ka raasta khula hai: \(u = 1 + e^x\).
Substitution ke baad \(\int \ln u\,du\) bachega, jo Question 1 mein hum parts se nikal chuke hain.
Plan: substitution, phir parts (ln \(\times\) 1), phir wapas \(x\) mein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int e^x\ln(1 + e^x)\,dx\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(u = 1 + e^x\) rakhenge, \(du = e^x\,dx\); phir \(\int \ln u\,du\) parts se (Question 1 ki tarah).

Substitution
\[u = 1 + e^x \Rightarrow du = e^x\,dx\]
\[\int e^x\ln(1 + e^x)\,dx = \int \ln u\,du\]
Kyun: \(e^x\,dx\) bilkul \(du\) ban gaya aur \(\ln(1 + e^x)\) ban gaya \(\ln u\). Integral bohat saaf ho gaya.

Parts: \(\ln u \cdot 1\)
\[= u\ln u - \int u\cdot\dfrac{1}{u}\,du\]
\[= u\ln u - u + c_1\]
Kyun: Question 1 wali chaal: \(\ln u\) first, 1 second; andar \(u\cdot\frac{1}{u} = 1\) reh gaya.

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[= (1 + e^x)\ln(1 + e^x) - (1 + e^x) + c_1\]
\[= (e^x + 1)\ln(1 + e^x) - e^x + c\]
Kyun: \(u = 1 + e^x\) wapas rakha. \(-(1 + e^x)\) mein se \(-1\) ek constant hai, usay \(c_1\) ke saath mila kar naya constant \(c = c_1 - 1\) bana diya. Is liye answer key wali shakal bhi sahi hai.
Dhyan dein: dono jawab, \(-(1 + e^x)\) wala aur \(-e^x\) wala, sahi hain; farq sirf constant ka hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[(e^x + 1)\ln(1 + e^x) - e^x\right]\]
\[= e^x\ln(1 + e^x) + (e^x + 1)\dfrac{e^x}{1 + e^x} - e^x\]
\[= e^x\ln(1 + e^x)\]
Kyun: product rule lagaya; \((e^x + 1)\) cancel ho kar \(e^x\) bacha jo \(-e^x\) se khatam ho gaya.
